name: Home services / trades trial sequences (a trade selling to commercial customers)
source: Copy v2 (docs/research/v2-leads-copy.md): for plumbing, roofing, HVAC, electrical, cleaning, landscaping and other trades whose prospects are property managers, facility managers, offices and other businesses. Plain text, no links in email 1, one reply CTA, four touches. No claim about the client beyond {oneLiner} / {proof}.

problem-first.label: Problem first
problem-first.why: Names the pain every property or facility manager knows (small repairs waiting until they are big), then one line on the offer, then an easy question.

touches.subject: @variant

touches.body:
{FirstName}, one more thought.

The jobs that hurt are the ones that wait. A crew that turns up when it says it will keeps a small problem small.

Worth a short call to see if {ClientCompany} could be that crew for {Company}?

touches.subject: {niche} for {Company}
touches.body:
{FirstName}, a different angle.

Most {ICP} keep a short list of trades they trust for the jobs that cannot wait. Getting on that list is all {ClientCompany} is after.

Open to a 15-minute call next week?

{FirstName}, this is my last note so your inbox stays clear.

If {niche} work comes up at {Company} later, a one-line reply here is all it takes.

Should I close the file for now?

question-led.label: Question led
question-led.why: Asks how they handle the work today; either answer is easy to write back.

touches.subject: @variant

touches.body:
{FirstName}, asking because the answer tells me quickly whether this is worth your time.

If you already have a crew you like, no need to change. If not, {ClientCompany} would be glad to be the next one you try.

Which is it at {Company}?

touches.subject: backup crew
touches.body:
{FirstName}, one practical thought.

Even {ICP} with a trusted crew need a second name for the week that crew is booked solid.

Would it help to have {ClientCompany} on file for {Company}?

{FirstName}, this is my last note so your inbox stays clear.

If {niche} work comes up at {Company} later, a one-line reply here is all it takes.

Should I close the file for now?

quick-idea.label: Quick idea
quick-idea.why: One small, practical idea first (a yearly walk-through); the ask is to send what it covers.

touches.subject: @variant

touches.body:
{FirstName}, a walk-through like that is quick to do and easy to put off.

{ClientCompany} can book one in at a time that suits you.

Would that be useful for {Company}?
